summary: Intermittent SSE heartbeat echo causes client silence and missing final metadata
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long streaming sessions (SSE) the client receives rapid duplicate heartbeat events ("heartbeat" event payload repeated), followed immediately by an extended silence where the final metadata/event that signals completion never arrives. The client SDK (atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.3) treats the duplicate heartbeat as an idempotent keepalive but then drops into a reconnection backoff when no further framed events arrive, resulting in a missing final_chunk metadata and incomplete conversation state in the customer app.

Impact:
- Several AtlasHealth users see generated responses missing the final summary paragraph and end-of-stream metadata (conversation_id and token_count).
- Partial responses appear in the UI; customer re-requests cause duplicate content or incorrect conversation stitching.
- Affects a subset (~3-4%) of long-running sessions (>40s) in us-east production.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) behind Redwood edge-proxy cluster ep-us-east-3
- Customer SDK: atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.3 (browser: Chrome 114 on Linux)
- Models: gpt-4o-mini pinned by customer to v2026-02-15

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a chat stream using SSE with a multi-paragraph prompt (expected token stream > 60 tokens).
2) Let stream run for 45-120s. Occasionally the stream shows a repeated heartbeat event (two identical keepalive frames within ~200ms).
3) After the duplicate heartbeat, client experiences no more framed events; SDK triggers internal reconnect/backoff after its idle window and UI never receives final metadata block (closing markers).

Observed behavior:
- Logs show duplicate heartbeat events from the edge (two SSE comment/keepalive blocks back-to-back) followed by no further data for ~90s.
- Client logs: SDK sees keepalive twice, then raises IdleTimeout -> reconnect; on reconnect the resumed session returns a new conversation snapshot but missing previous final metadata.
- Redwood serving runtime traces show the worker completed token generation and sent final metadata to the edge upstream, but the edge cluster logs contain a short-lived connection handoff at the same timestamp as the duplicate heartbeat.

Expected behavior:
- Heartbeats should be single periodic keepalives that do not change resume state. Final metadata and end-of-stream markers should always be delivered once the worker completes generation, regardless of transient proxy/hand-off events.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge-proxy trace (ep-us-east-3) at 2026-03-13T18:22:11.123Z:
  "SSE_KEEPALIVE id=xyz123 ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.123Z"
  "SSE_KEEPALIVE id=xyz123 ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.326Z"
  "CONN_HANDOFF id=xyz123 from=ep-us-east-2 to=ep-us-east-3 reason=upstream_rebalance code=1001"
- SDK log (client):
  "keepalive:received (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.326Z)"
  "idle_timeout:triggered (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:13.450Z)"
  "reconnect:attempt 1 (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:13.450Z)"
- Serving runtime (worker-42):
  "generation.complete: session=abc789 total_tokens=138 final_meta_sent=true ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.190Z"

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between ep-proxy connection handoff and heartbeat emission causes the edge to send a duplicate keepalive while simultaneously tearing over the socket, which results in the handoff path not forwarding the final metadata. Edge logs show handoff and duplicate keepalive within a ~250ms window.
- Client SDK's idle/backoff timer is more aggressive than the end-to-end delivery guarantees in presence of connection handoff; duplicate heartbeat may confuse client-side reassembly logic in older SDK versions.

Immediate customer impact and workaround:
- AtlasHealth has implemented a temporary client-side patch (delay idle timeout to 6s from 2s) to reduce false reconnects. This reduces but does not eliminate missing finals.

Next steps proposed:
- SRE to correlate edge handoff logs with specific proxy instances and flag candidate misconfigured keepalive behavior.
- Runtime team to verify that final metadata is forwarded reliably across handoff.
- SDK team to add defend logic for duplicate immediate-heartbeat sequences (treat as single keepalive and extend local idle window for a short period).
comments: 2026-03-13 18:30 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Opening incident and escalated to SRE. Assigned Liam for investigation.

2026-03-13 18:45 UTC - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Replicated one occurrence in staging by forcing ep-proxy rebalancer to rotate an active connection; saw duplicate keepalive emitted by old proxy before shut down. Attaching trace IDs privately.

2026-03-13 19:05 UTC - Priya Menon (Runtime): Checked worker logs for session abc789; worker claims final_meta_sent=true at 18:22:11.190Z, so generation completed prior to the duplicate heartbeat. Suggests the final metadata was delivered to upstream but not forwarded to the client after handoff.
2026-03-13 19:20 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports their temporary SDK patch reduced frequency from ~4% to ~0.8% of sessions. They prefer a server-side fix as long-term solution.

2026-03-14 08:10 UTC - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Running targeted test across ep-us-east-3 with controlled handoffs; observed 2/50 sessions missing final metadata when handoff overlapped with keepalive emission. Creating a kernel-level ticket for proxy behavior tuning.

2026-03-14 10:00 UTC - Elena García (Edge team): Found edge config that emits keepalive on close path and also on scheduled interval; in race both were emitted. Preparing a config patch to deduplicate keepalive on close path and to buffer final telemetry until forward ACK.
investigation_notes: Edge handoff events co-locate with duplicate keepalive frames in ~100ms window — strong correlate to observed client missing finals.
Serving runtime reliably marks final metadata as sent to upstream; problem reproduces when edge fails to forward final metadata after a handoff sequence.
Client SDK v2.1.3 reacts to repeated heartbeat then idle: SDK's internal reconnect threshold is 2s; raising helped but not complete mitigation.
Staging rebalancer test increased handoff rate and reproduced missing final metadata in ~4% of forced handoffs; suggests non-negligible race condition.
No evidence of model worker crash or retry — generation completes normally.
No billing discrepancies observed — token accounting is recorded on server side for affected sessions.
resolution_notes: EDGE: rolling out a config patch to deduplicate immediate successive keepalive sends from the same connection context (edge commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/commit/abc123).

EDGE: adding a short buffering window (250ms) to wait for final metadata forwarding to finish before emitting connection-close on handoff. Controlled rollout to ep-us-east-3 beginning 2026-03-14T18:00Z.

SDK: created ticket INT-4555 for atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.4 which will treat back-to-back keepalives within 500ms as a single event and temporarily extend idle window by 1.5x when duplicate keepalive seen. Patch is backward compatible.

Follow-up: monitor SUP-128001 for 72 hours after edge patch rollout; customer to confirm reduction to <0.2% incidence. If not resolved, plan deeper tcp socket lifecycle tracing on proxy (separate ticket).
